headline: The Water Is Back. Arcturus Isn't.
body:
[[The Shelf]]'s lower-deck drainage system failed on the night of February 11th. Most of you know this because you spent February 12th moving your floor-level possessions to higher shelves and arguing about whose bucket was whose. For those who were not here: Level 3 through Level 7 between [[Kit Haugen|Anchor]] Block and the old sorting facility took on approximately 40 centimeters of standing water over an eight-hour period. The drainage sump that should have handled it has not been serviced since 2221. The maintenance contract — held by a subsidiary of a subsidiary of a company that might technically be Arcturus Civil Security, nobody is entirely sure — expired in November and was not renewed. The notice of non-renewal was filed with the zone authority. The zone authority forwarded it to the relevant municipal desk. The municipal desk forwarded it to the relevant tier-infrastructure division. The tier-infrastructure division is currently six months behind on all non-emergency correspondence.

[[Soren Sokolov|Nobody]] came.

What did happen: the building committee on Level 9 organized a bucket chain. The residents of Level 4 in Block 7 who have the communal pump — the one they pooled for after the last flooding two years ago — ran it for fourteen straight hours. [[Kira Chakraborty-Vongphasouk|Yemi]] Koffi-Santos from Level 6, who worked drainage systems before she came to the [[GLMZ|Glooms]], spent all of February 12th crawling through the sump access tunnels identifying which valves could be manually forced and which ones were seized beyond moving. By morning of the 13th the water was down to 12 centimeters. By evening it was mostly gone.

We are writing this down because things that happen in the [[GLMZ|Glooms]] do not get written down unless we write them ourselves. The flooding happened. The building committee handled it. Arcturus did not appear. The zone authority did not appear. The tier-infrastructure division will receive a formal incident report this week and will send an automated acknowledgment within 30 days and will schedule a site visit sometime in the next 14 to 36 months, which is the stated response window for Review Category 4 infrastructure incidents, which is what they call it when the people affected are below Tier 2 and there are no corp-adjacent properties in the flood zone.

If you are on Level 3 through 5 in the [[Kit Haugen|Anchor]] Block area: the floor-level seals on at least two utility access panels were damaged in the flooding and will not reseal properly. This is a security issue as well as a structural one. Tell your block committee. Do not wait for someone else to tell them.

[[GLMZ|The Glooms]] takes care of its own. This has always been true. We are writing it down anyway, because the record exists even when nobody reads it, and someday someone will want to know how many times the zone authority was notified before something worse happened.
aftermath: The building committee's incident report received an automated acknowledgment from the GLMZ Tier Infrastructure Division on March 3rd, 2225. No inspector was dispatched. On April 18th, 2225, the TID issued a second automated notice assigning the report to Review Category 4 — Deferred Infrastructure Assessment, with an estimated response timeline of 14 to 36 months. The Glooms Dispatch published both automated responses in full.
runner_relevance: Lower-tier flooding events generate consistent runner work in the Glooms: residents hire couriers to file simultaneous documentation across multiple authority levels, since single filings reliably disappear; community organizers need materials moved when official channels fail; and the gap in corporate security coverage during infrastructure failures creates windows for protection contracts and for parties who need to move through a block without being observed. The community pump network — informal equipment pooled by block-level collectives — is also a useful resource map for operators who need to know which blocks have maintained off-grid infrastructure.
